title: Melanoma (cutaneous)
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE navigator (draft)
provenanceNote: DRAFT decision support authored from standard oncology references (NCCN/DeVita/Harrison) in the author's own words - the physician decides and the existing dose engine computes patient doses. Full cutaneous-melanoma pathway: diagnosis / subtype, workup and pathologic microstaging, molecular testing, AJCC staging and risk stratification, then stage-directed and biomarker-directed (BRAF V600) treatment. Every major arm is refined before a recommendation: localized disease routes through sentinel-node staging then risk-adapted adjuvant to surveillance; resectable stage III routes through a neoadjuvant-vs-upfront decision with response-adapted adjuvant escalation; advanced disease is a line-of-therapy sub-tree (first line -> on-progression question -> second line -> on-progression -> later line) for each of the BRAF-mutant (immunotherapy-first vs targeted-first) and BRAF wild-type (combination vs single-agent) subgroups; brain metastases and in-transit disease feed the same systemic lines; a recurrence pathway re-enters by relapse pattern. Treatment leaves route to APPLICABLE existing StewardMD Standard Protocols by reference; surgery, radiation, and local therapies (T-VEC, isolated limb infusion / perfusion, radiosurgery) are checklist guidance with NO dose. No proprietary guideline text reproduced; invents no dose / regimen. DRAFT - not clinically activated.
sourceNote: Structural pathway consistent with standard oncology references (NCCN / DeVita / Harrison), Cutaneous Melanoma. Regimen options reference existing StewardMD Standard Protocols; the dose engine computes patient doses.

a.text: Sentinel lymph node biopsy is generally discussed for a Breslow thickness at or above 0.8 mm, or for any ulcerated primary, and offered after a shared risk / benefit conversation; it is staging (not therapeutic) and is not needed for pure in-situ disease.

b.text: Adjuvant anti-PD-1 (nivolumab or pembrolizumab) and, for BRAF V600-mutant resected disease, adjuvant dabrafenib plus trametinib each reduce recurrence risk in resected stage III; the absolute benefit is weighed against immune-related or targeted-therapy toxicity and patient preference.

c.text: Combination nivolumab plus ipilimumab yields higher response rates and meaningful intracranial activity in asymptomatic brain metastases, at the cost of substantially more grade 3-4 immune-related toxicity than single-agent anti-PD-1.

d.text: BRAF / MEK targeted therapy produces rapid, high-rate responses useful for symptomatic or high-burden disease, but immunotherapy responses are more often durable; first-line sequencing in BRAF-mutant disease is individualized, and the class not used first is generally held for the next line.

e.text: After neoadjuvant checkpoint therapy, the pathologic response on the resection specimen is prognostic: a major or complete pathologic response predicts excellent outcome and supports de-escalated adjuvant therapy, whereas substantial residual viable tumor supports switching or intensifying adjuvant treatment.

nodes.name: Diagnosis
nodes.title: Cutaneous melanoma: histologic subtype
nodes.description: Confirmed cutaneous melanoma on biopsy. Note the subtype; management then follows depth and stage, not subtype, for most decisions.
bullets: Superficial spreading (most common)
Nodular (often thicker at presentation)
Lentigo maligna (chronically sun-damaged skin)
Acral lentiginous (palms, soles, subungual; consider KIT testing)
Desmoplastic (neurotropic; sentinel-node yield is lower)

nodes.name: Initial workup
nodes.title: Initial workup
nodes.description: Establish local extent, screen for regional and distant spread, and gather baseline data before staging.
bullets: Full history and complete skin and regional lymph-node examination; document any satellite or in-transit lesions
Review the excisional / diagnostic biopsy pathology (see microstaging)
Photograph and map the primary site; note prior lesions and second primaries
Baseline labs including LDH for higher-stage disease
Cross-sectional imaging (CT or PET/CT) reserved for node-positive or symptomatic / high-risk disease, not routine for thin node-negative primaries

nodes.name: Microstaging
nodes.title: Pathologic microstaging
nodes.description: The primary tumor's pathology drives T category, sentinel-node decisions, and prognosis.
bullets: Breslow thickness (mm) - the dominant primary-tumor prognostic factor
Ulceration present or absent (upstages within each T category)
Dermal mitotic rate
Deep and peripheral margin status on the diagnostic specimen
Microsatellites, lymphovascular invasion, and perineural invasion if reported

nodes.name: Molecular testing
nodes.title: Molecular testing
nodes.description: Molecular results guide systemic-therapy eligibility, chiefly BRAF V600 status. Testing is essential for resected stage III and for advanced disease; it is not required for localized, node-negative disease that will only be excised.
bullets: BRAF V600 (E/K) mutation testing - enables BRAF / MEK targeted therapy
Consider NRAS and, for acral / mucosal primaries, KIT testing (largely trial-directed)
Send tissue for testing at diagnosis of stage III / IV so results are ready when systemic therapy is chosen

nodes.name: AJCC staging
nodes.title: AJCC staging and risk stratification
nodes.description: Assign an AJCC stage group from T (Breslow / ulceration), N (nodal / in-transit), and M (distant). Select the applicable category to route treatment.

nodes.name: In situ
nodes.title: Melanoma in situ: wide excision
nodes.description: Local surgery is curative; no nodal staging or systemic therapy. Route to lifelong skin surveillance.
bullets: Wide local excision with roughly 0.5-1.0 cm clinical margins to a clear deep plane
No sentinel lymph node biopsy for pure in-situ disease
Consider staged excision or topical / radiation options for broad lentigo maligna where surgery is difficult
No systemic therapy; proceed to skin surveillance

nodes.name: Localized surgery
nodes.title: Stage I-II: wide local excision
nodes.description: Wide local excision with margins scaled to Breslow thickness, then a sentinel-node decision.

tables.title: Recommended clinical excision margin by Breslow thickness

options.label: Excision planned - proceed to nodal staging

nodes.name: SLNB
nodes.title: Sentinel lymph node biopsy
nodes.description: Sentinel-node status is the strongest regional prognostic factor and determines whether disease is upstaged to stage III.
bullets: Discuss SLNB for Breslow at or above 0.8 mm, or for any ulcerated primary
Not required for thin, non-ulcerated, low-mitotic T1a lesions
Perform at the time of wide excision when feasible

nodes.name: Node-negative risk
nodes.title: Node-negative (stage I-II): primary-tumor risk
nodes.description: After a negative sentinel node, the primary-tumor T category stratifies risk. Low-risk disease goes directly to surveillance; resected high-risk stage IIB-IIC now has an adjuvant immunotherapy option.

nodes.name: Stage II adjuvant IO
nodes.title: High-risk stage IIB-IIC: adjuvant anti-PD-1
nodes.description: Adjuvant checkpoint immunotherapy reduces recurrence in resected high-risk node-negative disease, then surveillance.
bullets: Adjuvant pembrolizumab (or nivolumab) for about one year after complete wide excision
Discuss the modest absolute recurrence-free-survival gain against immune-related toxicity
Observation with close surveillance remains a reasonable alternative after shared decision-making
Baseline thyroid / endocrine and organ-function labs before starting

nodes.name: Resectability
nodes.title: Stage III: resectability
nodes.description: Determine whether nodal / regional disease can be completely resected; unresectable disease is treated as advanced.

nodes.name: Neoadjuvant
nodes.title: Resectable stage III: neoadjuvant option
nodes.description: For bulky clinically-node-positive disease, neoadjuvant immunotherapy before definitive surgery improves event-free survival and is increasingly preferred; otherwise proceed straight to surgery.

nodes.name: Neoadjuvant IO
nodes.title: Neoadjuvant immunotherapy, then lymph-node surgery
nodes.description: A short course of checkpoint immunotherapy before definitive lymph-node dissection; pathologic response on the resection specimen guides subsequent adjuvant therapy.
bullets: Neoadjuvant anti-PD-1 (pembrolizumab-based) or nivolumab plus ipilimumab for a limited number of cycles
Then wide local excision of the primary and therapeutic lymph-node dissection
The pathologic response drives the next step (response-adapted adjuvant)
Monitor for immune-related toxicity that could delay surgery

nodes.name: Path response
nodes.title: After neoadjuvant + surgery: pathologic response
nodes.description: The pathologic response on the resection specimen is response-adapted: a major / complete response supports de-escalated adjuvant therapy, while significant residual viable tumor supports switching or intensifying.

nodes.name: Responder adjuvant
nodes.title: Major pathologic response: complete / de-escalated adjuvant anti-PD-1
nodes.description: A major or complete pathologic response predicts excellent outcome; complete the planned anti-PD-1 course, then surveillance.
bullets: Complete adjuvant anti-PD-1 (nivolumab or pembrolizumab) to about one year total therapy
De-escalation / early stopping is under study; individualize duration
No routine switch to targeted therapy given the favorable response
Continue immune-toxicity monitoring, then risk-adapted surveillance

nodes.name: Residual adjuvant
nodes.title: Residual viable tumor: switch / intensify adjuvant therapy
nodes.description: Significant residual tumor after neoadjuvant immunotherapy predicts higher relapse risk and supports changing the adjuvant strategy.
bullets: For BRAF V600-mutant disease, switch to adjuvant dabrafenib plus trametinib
For BRAF wild-type disease, complete / continue adjuvant anti-PD-1 (or enroll on a trial of intensification)
Consider adjuvant nodal-basin radiation only for selected high-risk pathologic features
Closer imaging surveillance given elevated relapse risk

nodes.name: Nodal surgery
nodes.title: Stage III (upfront): definitive surgery and nodal management
nodes.description: Complete the primary excision and manage the nodal basin, then decide adjuvant systemic therapy by BRAF status.
bullets: Wide local excision of the primary with stage-appropriate margins
For a positive sentinel node, nodal ultrasound surveillance is an accepted alternative to completion lymph-node dissection
Therapeutic lymph-node dissection for clinically / radiologically involved nodes
Consider adjuvant radiation to the basin only for selected high-risk features

nodes.name: Adjuvant BRAF
nodes.title: Resected stage III: BRAF status for adjuvant choice
nodes.description: BRAF V600 status opens targeted adjuvant therapy in addition to immunotherapy.

nodes.name: Adjuvant IO
nodes.title: Adjuvant anti-PD-1 immunotherapy (BRAF wild-type)
nodes.description: Checkpoint immunotherapy reduces recurrence after complete resection of stage III disease, then surveillance.
bullets: Adjuvant nivolumab or pembrolizumab for about one year
Monitor for immune-related adverse events (thyroid, colitis, hepatitis, pneumonitis, endocrinopathy)
Observation is reasonable for the lowest-risk resected stage III after shared decision-making
Then risk-adapted surveillance

nodes.name: Adjuvant BRAF/MEK
nodes.title: Adjuvant BRAF / MEK or anti-PD-1 (BRAF-mutant)
nodes.description: BRAF V600-mutant resected stage III can receive adjuvant targeted therapy or adjuvant immunotherapy, then surveillance.
bullets: Adjuvant dabrafenib plus trametinib for about one year, or
Adjuvant anti-PD-1 (nivolumab or pembrolizumab)
Targeted therapy causes pyrexia, arthralgia, and transaminitis; immunotherapy causes immune-related events - factor comorbidity and preference
Then risk-adapted surveillance

nodes.name: In-transit
nodes.title: In-transit / satellite disease: burden
nodes.description: Regionally confined non-nodal spread. Burden and resectability decide between local control and systemic therapy.

nodes.name: In-transit local
nodes.title: Limited in-transit disease: local therapy
nodes.description: Isolated, resectable in-transit lesions are managed with local control, then surveillance.
bullets: Complete surgical excision of isolated lesions to negative margins when feasible
Intralesional talimogene laherparepvec (T-VEC) for accessible cutaneous / subcutaneous lesions
Radiation for a symptomatic unresectable lesion
Then close surveillance for further in-transit or nodal spread

nodes.name: In-transit systemic
nodes.title: Extensive in-transit disease: systemic + regional therapy
nodes.description: Extensive or unresectable limb / in-transit disease is treated with systemic immunotherapy and regional techniques; on progression it enters the advanced line-of-therapy pathway.
bullets: Systemic checkpoint immunotherapy (anti-PD-1, or nivolumab plus ipilimumab for higher burden)
Isolated limb infusion / perfusion for extensive limb disease at experienced centers
Intralesional T-VEC for accessible lesions as an adjunct
Reassess response; progression routes to the advanced systemic-therapy pathway

nodes.name: In-transit response
nodes.title: In-transit disease: response to systemic therapy
nodes.description: Response-adapted branch after systemic therapy for extensive in-transit disease.

nodes.name: Advanced workup
nodes.title: Advanced / metastatic workup
nodes.description: Define disease extent and biomarkers before systemic therapy for unresectable stage III or stage IV disease.
bullets: LDH and organ-function labs (LDH is prognostic and defines M1 substage)
Whole-body PET/CT or CT chest / abdomen / pelvis
Brain MRI - required, as melanoma has a high propensity for CNS spread
Confirm BRAF V600 status (test now if not already done); consider broader NGS

nodes.name: Brain mets
nodes.title: Brain metastases present?
nodes.description: CNS involvement adds local-therapy decisions but still routes into the systemic line-of-therapy pathway.

nodes.name: Brain mgmt
nodes.title: Brain metastases: symptom status
nodes.description: Symptom burden and lesion size determine whether upfront local therapy is needed alongside systemic treatment.

nodes.name: Brain systemic
nodes.title: Asymptomatic brain mets: upfront combination immunotherapy
nodes.description: Combination checkpoint immunotherapy has meaningful intracranial activity and can be used before local therapy in asymptomatic disease; then define BRAF status for the systemic line-of-therapy plan.
bullets: Nivolumab plus ipilimumab for asymptomatic, steroid-independent brain metastases
Consider stereotactic radiosurgery for lesions that persist or progress
Serial brain MRI to monitor intracranial response
Then proceed on the systemic (BRAF-directed) line-of-therapy pathway

nodes.name: Brain local
nodes.title: Symptomatic brain mets: local therapy then systemic
nodes.description: Symptomatic or large lesions need local control first; then continue on the systemic line-of-therapy pathway.
bullets: Stereotactic radiosurgery for limited lesions, or surgery for a large / dominant symptomatic lesion
Whole-brain radiation reserved for extensive disease
Corticosteroids for symptomatic edema (note steroids blunt immunotherapy)
Once stabilized, proceed on the systemic (BRAF-directed) line-of-therapy pathway

nodes.name: Advanced BRAF
nodes.title: Advanced disease: BRAF V600 status
nodes.description: BRAF V600 status determines whether targeted therapy is available alongside immunotherapy for first-line and subsequent systemic therapy.

nodes.name: Mutant first line
nodes.title: BRAF-mutant advanced: first-line strategy
nodes.description: Both immunotherapy and BRAF / MEK targeted therapy are first-line options; choose by pace of disease, symptoms, and toxicity tolerance. The class not used first is generally held for second line.

tables.title: First-line options in BRAF V600-mutant advanced melanoma
rows: Fit for immune toxicity, lower burden
High burden / symptomatic, need quick control

nodes.name: Mutant IO 1L
nodes.title: BRAF-mutant: first-line immunotherapy
nodes.description: Checkpoint immunotherapy as the first systemic therapy in BRAF-mutant advanced disease; targeted therapy is held for progression.
bullets: Combination nivolumab plus ipilimumab for higher response, or single-agent anti-PD-1 for a gentler toxicity profile
Reserve BRAF / MEK therapy for later progression
Monitor closely for immune-related toxicity
Reassess with imaging; progression routes to second-line targeted therapy

nodes.name: Mutant 1L IO response
nodes.title: BRAF-mutant after first-line immunotherapy: response
nodes.description: Response-adapted: continue and monitor a responder, or switch class on progression.

options.label: Response / durable control - continue and monitor

nodes.name: Mutant targeted 2L
nodes.title: BRAF-mutant second line: BRAF / MEK targeted therapy
nodes.description: On progression after first-line immunotherapy, switch class to BRAF plus MEK inhibition.
bullets: Dabrafenib plus trametinib (a BRAF / MEK combination) for rapid, high-rate responses
Useful when disease is now bulky or symptomatic and quick control is needed
Watch for pyrexia, cutaneous events, and transaminitis; plan for eventual resistance
Reassess; further progression routes to later-line options

nodes.name: Mutant 2L response
nodes.title: BRAF-mutant after second line: response
nodes.description: Response-adapted branch after second-line therapy in BRAF-mutant disease.

options.label: Response / disease controlled - continue and monitor

nodes.name: Mutant targeted 1L
nodes.title: BRAF-mutant: first-line targeted therapy
nodes.description: BRAF plus MEK inhibition for rapid control of BRAF V600-mutant disease; immunotherapy is held for progression.
bullets: Dabrafenib plus trametinib (a BRAF / MEK combination) for rapid, high-rate responses
Preferred when disease is bulky or symptomatic and quick control is needed
Watch for pyrexia, cutaneous events, and transaminitis; plan for eventual resistance
Reassess with imaging; progression routes to second-line immunotherapy

nodes.name: Mutant 1L targeted response
nodes.title: BRAF-mutant after first-line targeted: response
nodes.description: Response-adapted: continue a responder, or switch class to immunotherapy on progression.

options.label: Response / durable control - continue and monitor

nodes.name: Mutant IO 2L
nodes.title: BRAF-mutant second line: immunotherapy
nodes.description: On progression after first-line targeted therapy, switch class to checkpoint immunotherapy.
bullets: Nivolumab plus ipilimumab for higher response, or single-agent anti-PD-1 by fitness / toxicity tolerance
Best started before the patient deteriorates, given slower onset of immune response
Monitor closely for immune-related toxicity
Reassess; further progression routes to later-line options

nodes.name: Mutant 2L IO response
nodes.title: BRAF-mutant after second-line immunotherapy: response
nodes.description: Response-adapted branch after second-line immunotherapy in BRAF-mutant disease.

options.label: Response / disease controlled - continue and monitor

nodes.name: WT first line
nodes.title: BRAF wild-type advanced: first-line strategy
nodes.description: Immunotherapy is the backbone; choose combination versus single-agent by risk, burden, and ability to tolerate toxicity.

nodes.name: WT combo 1L
nodes.title: BRAF wild-type: first-line combination immunotherapy
nodes.description: Dual checkpoint blockade for higher response in fit patients.
bullets: Nivolumab plus ipilimumab for higher response rates, weighed against more grade 3-4 immune toxicity
Favored for higher burden or aggressive disease in patients able to tolerate combination toxicity
Structured immune-toxicity monitoring and prompt steroid management
Reassess with imaging; progression routes to second-line options

nodes.name: WT combo response
nodes.title: BRAF wild-type after first-line combination: response
nodes.description: Response-adapted: continue a responder, or move to second line on progression.

options.label: Response / durable control - continue and monitor

nodes.name: WT 2L
nodes.title: BRAF wild-type second line
nodes.description: Options after progression on first-line immunotherapy in BRAF wild-type disease.
bullets: Tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) therapy (lifileucel) at experienced centers for anti-PD-1-refractory disease
Alternate anti-PD-1-based regimen or a clinical trial (e.g. LAG-3 combination)
For KIT-mutant acral / mucosal disease, consider a KIT inhibitor (trial-directed)
Reassess; further progression routes to later-line options

nodes.name: WT 2L response
nodes.title: BRAF wild-type after second line: response
nodes.description: Response-adapted branch after second-line therapy in BRAF wild-type disease.

options.label: Response / disease controlled - continue and monitor

nodes.name: WT mono 1L
nodes.title: BRAF wild-type: first-line single-agent anti-PD-1
nodes.description: Single-agent checkpoint inhibition with a more favorable toxicity profile.
bullets: Nivolumab or pembrolizumab monotherapy
Preferred when combination toxicity is a concern or comorbidity limits tolerance
Monitor for immune-related adverse events
Reassess with imaging; progression allows escalation to combination immunotherapy

nodes.name: WT mono response
nodes.title: BRAF wild-type after first-line single-agent: response
nodes.description: Response-adapted: continue a responder, or escalate to combination immunotherapy on progression.

options.label: Response / durable control - continue and monitor

nodes.name: WT mono 2L
nodes.title: BRAF wild-type second line: escalate to combination immunotherapy
nodes.description: On progression after single-agent anti-PD-1, escalate to dual checkpoint blockade, then reassess.
bullets: Nivolumab plus ipilimumab in patients fit for combination toxicity
Structured immune-toxicity monitoring and prompt steroid management
Consider TIL therapy or a clinical trial if not a combination candidate
Reassess; further progression routes to later-line options

nodes.name: Later line
nodes.title: Later-line / refractory advanced disease
nodes.description: Options after both immunotherapy and (where applicable) targeted therapy have been used.
bullets: Clinical trial enrollment is preferred where available
Tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) therapy (lifileucel) for immunotherapy-refractory disease at experienced centers
BRAF / MEK rechallenge in BRAF-mutant disease after a prior response and treatment interval
Cytotoxic chemotherapy or best supportive care for refractory disease; palliative radiation for symptomatic sites
Then continue supportive surveillance

nodes.name: Surveillance
nodes.title: Surveillance / follow-up
nodes.description: Risk-adapted follow-up after curative-intent or disease-controlling therapy.
bullets: History with full skin and lymph-node exam every 3-12 months, intensity scaled to stage, then annually long-term
Patient education on monthly skin self-exam and sun protection
Cross-sectional / brain imaging for higher-risk resected disease per risk; not routine for low-risk stage I-II
Lifelong annual skin surveillance (elevated second-primary risk)
nodes.linkLabel: If recurrence is detected: go to the Recurrence pathway

nodes.name: Recurrence
nodes.title: Recurrence pattern
nodes.description: Route by the pattern of relapse.

nodes.name: Local recurrence
nodes.title: Local / in-transit recurrence
nodes.description: Re-establish local control; escalate to systemic therapy if disease is widespread.
bullets: Re-excise resectable local or in-transit recurrence to negative margins
Intralesional T-VEC, isolated limb infusion / perfusion, or radiation for multifocal limb disease
Restage; move to the advanced pathway if distant spread is found
Consider systemic immunotherapy for unresectable or rapidly recurring disease, then surveillance
